267366284_a1c0674b.text: Using immunohistochemistry of the transcription factor Phox2a specifically expressed in noradrenergic neurons (Goridis et al., 1999)(Morin et al., 1997)(Yang et al., 1998) (Fig. 5A), we measured the surface of the Locus Coeruleus (data not shown) and the density of noradrenergic neurons (Fig. 5B)

267366284_bb2513d7.text: .Similar densities of Tyrosine Hydroxylase positive cells (TH, enzyme required for NA synthesis and marker of NA neurons) were also found in the Locus Coeruleus of enriched and control mice (Fig. 5A and C, see Table 5 for detailed statistical results). Moreover, "resting-noradrenergic" neurons exist in the rostral Locus Coeruleus under basal conditions. These neurons express the Phox2a transcription factor but not TH and can be reactivated following treatment with RU 24722 (a catecholaminergic activator) (Bezin et al., 2000).
